questions.q:
The Supreme Court's 2025 directions in State of U.P. v. Ajmal Beg sought better enforcement of anti-dowry law. Consider the following statements:
1. Under the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, property qualifies as dowry only if it is given on the wedding day.
2. Dowry Prohibition Officers are appointed by State Governments.
3. The Court asked High Courts to take stock of pending cases of dowry death and of cruelty.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Dowry Prohibition Officers are a State responsibility, and the Court wanted them trained and their contact details publicised. Statement 1 is wrong: the statute covers property given or agreed to be given at, before or any time after marriage, and Satvir Singh (2001) likewise looked at the link with marriage rather than timing. The directions also addressed police training.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The migration rate reported by PLFS 2020-21 is much higher for women than for men.
Statement-II: Marriage is the main reason for women's migration, whereas employment is the main reason for men's.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is not correct
Statement-I is not correct but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are true and the second explains the gap. Social practice of women moving to the husband's place drives a high female rate, with marriage accounting for about 86.8 per cent. For men, employment is the leading reason. The National Statistics Office's coming survey can help separate such movements from labour migration and so give better data for designing portable welfare.

questions.q:
Match the following Supreme Court decisions with the principle associated with them:
List-I
A. Satvir Singh v. State of Punjab (2001)
B. Rajbir v. State of Haryana (2010)
C. Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar (2014)
List-II
1. Property given in connection with marriage is dowry regardless of when demanded
2. Trial courts asked to add the murder charge in dowry-death cases unless evidence shows otherwise
3. No automatic arrest for cruelty; police must record reasons and a Magistrate must be satisfied
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: The three cases address different stages. Satvir Singh widened the meaning of dowry through its connection with marriage. Rajbir addressed framing of charges, directing courts to add the murder section alongside dowry death. Arnesh Kumar dealt with arrest powers under the cruelty provision, and warned Magistrates authorising detention mechanically. Reading them together shows courts balancing protection for victims and safeguards for the accused.

questions.q:
A Nagaland University review explained how the body's immune cells can aid breast cancer. Consider the following statements:
1. M1 macrophages are the state that cancer cells promote because they build new blood vessels for the tumour.
2. Tumour-associated macrophages can suppress T cells.
3. Cancer cells can display 'don't eat me' signals that stop macrophages attacking them.
4. Remodelling of the extracellular matrix by such macrophages eases invasion.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct, showing how tumours co-opt immunity and spread. Statement 1 is wrong because M1 is the anti-tumour, pro-inflammatory state. Cancer pushes macrophages towards M2, a tissue-repair state whose cytokines drive angiogenesis, supplying oxygen and nutrients. Hence therapies under study seek to re-educate macrophages back to M1 and block signals that convert them, alongside chemotherapy or radiotherapy.

questions.q:
With reference to breast cancer biology and treatment, consider the following statements:
1. Inherited BRCA1 and BRCA2 gene mutations raise the risk of the disease.
2. HER2-positive tumours can be treated with targeted therapy.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are correct. BRCA genes normally help repair DNA, so harmful mutations raise cancer risk and are why family history matters. HER2 is a growth-signalling receptor, and tumours overexpressing it respond to therapy aimed at that protein. Hormone therapy, by contrast, blocks oestrogen. Screening by mammogram helps detection early, which is valuable before an invasive tumour spreads to lymph nodes and other organs.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 23-25; BRCA function is static

questions.q:
The debate on banning social media for children under 16 turned attention to Indian law. Consider the following statements:
1. Section 79 of the Information Technology Act, 2000 provides safe harbour for intermediaries who observe due diligence.
2. The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 treats persons below 16 years as children for its consent provisions.
3. The IT (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021 provide for grievance redressal and compliance officers.
Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Safe harbour shields platforms from liability for user content when they meet due-diligence duties, and the 2021 Rules add grievance and takedown processes. Statement 2 is wrong because the 2023 Act defines a child as a person below 18 and requires verifiable parental consent; critics argue such consent gating could cause false declarations or exclusion of young users.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 8-10; DPDP age threshold is static

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about under-16 social media curbs abroad, as reported in February 2026, is correct?
o: France was the first country to enforce such a ban, and Australia later copied the model with criminal liability for executives.
Australia's law requires parents, and not platforms, to verify the age of each user.
Spain announced plans for a ban with criminal liability for executives, while Australia had earlier become the first country to ban most social media for this age group.
Spain's plan requires platforms to obtain a licence from the European Commission.
questions.e: Australia moved first, requiring platforms themselves to verify age and disable underage accounts, so the burden falls on companies. Spain's February 2026 plan is distinctive for its executive liability. France, the UK and the Netherlands are among countries weighing curbs, not leading enforcement. Critics in India argue such bans are porous and push users to VPNs and unmonitored spaces, besides raising identity-linked surveillance risks.

questions.q:
With reference to the criminal law on dowry after the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, consider the following statements:
1. Dowry death, earlier under Section 304-B of the IPC, is now in Section 80 of the Sanhita.
2. Cruelty by a husband or his relatives, earlier Section 498-A of the IPC, is now in Section 103 of the Sanhita.
3. A death qualifies as dowry death only if it occurs within one year of the marriage.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: cruelty has moved to Section 85, while Section 103 is the murder provision that replaced IPC 302. Statement 3 is wrong as the period is seven years of marriage, along with evidence that the woman faced cruelty or harassment for dowry soon before her death. The offence is treated seriously, with a minimum term of seven years.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 81-82; seven-year limb is static

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding India's digital economy and access gaps, as cited in February 2026:
1. The digital economy accounted for over one-tenth of GDP in 2022-23.
2. India hosts a small share of the world's Global Capability Centres, well behind the Philippines and Poland.
3. The National Sample Survey shows a marked gender gap in having ever used the Internet.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The share was 11.74 per cent, with digitally enabling industries as the largest part, and only 33.3 per cent of women against 57.1 per cent of men have ever used the Internet. Statement 2 is wrong as India is cited as hosting 55 per cent of the world's such centres, which are a big driver of the projected rise in share.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Critics hold that a blanket ban on social media for under-16s may hurt girls from low-income homes disproportionately.
Statement-II: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 already bars all users below 16 from social media platforms.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is not correct
Statement-I is not correct but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement I is a real objection: when household access is limited, girls are already less online, and a ban could further reduce their limited routes to information and networks. Statement II is false: the 2023 Act deals with consent for processing children's data and imposes no such ban; that is why the debate continues. Critics suggest instead a duty of care for big technology firms and an independent expert regulator.

questions.q:
With reference to women in STEM in India, consider the following statements:
1. Women form a substantial share of STEM enrolment in higher education, but far fewer stay in research careers.
2. WISE-KIRAN is a programme of the University Grants Commission providing free laptops to all girl students.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct, describing the 'leaky pipeline' from enrolment to career, with women at about 43 per cent of STEM enrolment. Statement 2 is wrong: WISE-KIRAN belongs to the Department of Science and Technology and supports women scientists, including those returning after breaks. Commentators argue such schemes do not change assumptions of a scientist as always available, ignoring unequal care work.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 22-23; WISE-KIRAN anchor is static

questions.q:
Which of the following are welfare or safety-net measures relevant to migrant workers, as cited with the migration survey?
1. One Nation One Ration Card
2. PM Shram Yogi Maan-Dhan
3. PM Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana
4. Transit-oriented Development
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Items 1, 2 and 3 are the safety nets. Ration portability lets migrants draw food entitlements anywhere, Maan-Dhan gives pension cover to unorganised workers, and the Anna Yojana provides free foodgrain. Item 4 is grouped instead with urban measures such as AMRUT and the Smart Cities Mission, since it concerns planning dense development around transit corridors and not direct welfare for individual migrants.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Macrophages are white blood cells that normally help remove harmful cells from the body.
Statement-II: Macrophages engulf and digest targets through phagocytosis.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is not correct
Statement-I is not correct but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct and the second gives the mechanism. In the tumour microenvironment, however, these same cells may turn into tumour-associated macrophages that aid the cancer. A self-reinforcing cycle follows: growing tumours recruit more macrophages, which further drive progression. Attention has thus shifted from tumour cells alone to the surrounding environment, supporting research on personalised, immune-based therapy that may be more precise and less toxic.

questions.q: The '4P approach' suggested for tackling dowry comprises:
o: Punishment, Protection, Prevention and Promotion of women's empowerment
questions.e: The approach treats dowry as a socio-economic institution rooted in patriarchy and marriage markets, not merely a legal problem. Punishment deters, protection supports victims, prevention changes norms and promotion empowers women. Prevention, Protection, Prosecution and Partnership is the framework used in anti-trafficking discussions, which is why it can confuse. The other two sets have no such use. Social sanctions and public recognition of dowry-free marriages complement this strategy locally.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 81-82; anti-trafficking parallel is static

questions.q:
With reference to the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, consider the following statements:
1. Only the taking of dowry is an offence; giving it is not.
2. All presents given at a wedding count as dowry, even if unsolicited and recorded in a list.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Neither is correct. Section 3 penalises both giving and taking, and abetting them as well, which is a reason why victims' families may hesitate to report. Statement 2 is wrong because the Act excludes presents given without demand if they are entered in a list kept under the rules. This is why the demand-and-connection test, not the gift itself, is central.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 81-82; Section 3 and its list exception are static

questions.q:
The migration survey raises questions about India's data bodies. Consider the following statements:
1. The National Statistics Office will run the Survey on Migration from July 2026.
2. The Periodic Labour Force Survey comes from the same statistical system under MoSPI.
3. The decennial Census is conducted by the National Statistics Office.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong because the Census is run by the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, who is under the Ministry of Home Affairs, whereas the National Statistics Office sits under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation. The distinction matters because migration figures come from both streams, with differing definitions, and so cannot be compared without care.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 83; Census authority is static

questions.q:
With reference to terms that appeared in reporting on breast cancer research, consider the following statements:
1. A mammogram is an X-ray-based screening test.
2. A carcinoma in situ remains at its site of origin, whereas an invasive one spreads to nearby tissue.
3. Angiogenesis means the destruction of blood vessels that feed a growing tumour.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Mammograms help early detection, and the in situ and invasive categories guide how aggressive treatment must be. Statement 3 is wrong as angiogenesis means forming new blood vessels, a process that supplies oxygen and nutrients to tumours. M2 macrophages release cytokines supporting this formation, which is why it is a target when researchers look at therapies acting on the tumour's surroundings.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 23-25; X-ray basis of mammography is static

questions.q:
The debate on regulating platforms for minors draws on existing internet law. Consider the following statements:
1. Shreya Singhal v. Union of India (2015) struck down Section 66A of the Information Technology Act, 2000.
2. Section 69A of the Act empowers the Central Government to direct the blocking of online content on specified grounds.
3. Shreya Singhal held that intermediaries must judge for themselves the legality of content and remove it upon any private complaint.
Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Section 66A failed for vagueness, while the blocking power survived because it has procedural safeguards. Statement 3 is wrong: the Court read Section 79 so that actual knowledge means a court order or government notification, sparing platforms from adjudicating private complaints. Critics in the current debate want to move past notice and takedown towards a duty of care.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 8-10; Shreya Singhal and Section 69A are static

questions.q: In discussions of India's digital economy in February 2026, 'GCC' refers to:
o: Global Capability Centres, the offshore units of multinational firms
the Gulf Cooperation Council of six West Asian states
the Grid Control Corporation that manages national load despatch
Government Cloud Computing under the MeghRaj initiative
questions.e: Here the term means Global Capability Centres, units that multinationals set up to perform technology and business functions, and India is said to host 55 per cent of them worldwide. The same acronym stands for the Gulf Cooperation Council in trade news, a clash noted this month. The other expansions are not used in this context, and they do not describe any driver cited.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs of a factor in migration and its classification:
1. Job opportunities at the destination : Pull factor
2. Natural calamities at the origin : Push factor
3. Low wages at the origin : Push factor
4. Prospect of a better life at the destination : Push factor
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are right. Pair 4 is wrong because the prospect of a better life attracts people to a destination, so it is a pull factor. Push factors are conditions at the origin that drive people out, such as lack of jobs and an unfavourable environment. Large outflows can reduce the rural workforce, while strain falls on urban health, education and transport.
